options.name: East to Jökulsárlón
options.note: Uses the 2 Nov half-day to drive back from Kirkjubæjarklaustur.

stops.note: Blue ice cave tour + Diamond Beach

options.name: No further east than Vík
options.note: Golden Circle first, then two nights in Vík.

places.name: Reykjavík centre
places.note: Base. Training venue and organisers' accommodation.
places.summary: Iceland's small, walkable capital and your base. Hallgrímskirkja church (lift to the tower), Harpa concert hall, the Sun Voyager sculpture and the Old Harbour are all within a 30-minute walk of each other.
facts: Free to wander; Hallgrímskirkja tower has a small fee
Geothermal pools (e.g. Sundhöllin, Vesturbæjarlaug) are cheap and very local
places.winter: Good aurora spot if you walk to the Grótta lighthouse, away from city lights.

places.name: Seljalandsfoss
places.note: You can walk behind the falls — waterproofs, and the path gets icy. Gljúfrabúi (hidden falls) is a short walk north.
places.summary: A slender ~60 m waterfall dropping over an old sea cliff right by the Ring Road. A path loops behind the curtain of water — you will get wet. Gljúfrabúi, a waterfall hidden inside a narrow canyon, is a 10-minute walk north.
places.winter: The path behind the falls is often closed or treacherous with ice — bring microspikes or just view from the front.

places.name: Skógafoss
places.note: Stairs up to a viewing platform on the right side.
places.summary: One of Iceland's biggest waterfalls: a 60 m high, 25 m wide wall of water you can walk right up to. A staircase of several hundred steps on the right leads to a viewing platform at the top, where the Fimmvörðuháls trail begins.
places.winter: The stairs can be icy. Spray freezes on the ground close to the falls.

places.name: Kvernufoss
places.note: 3 min from Skógafoss, almost always empty.
places.summary: A quieter waterfall in a mossy gorge just east of Skógar. A short walk from the parking near the Skógar Museum, and like Seljalandsfoss you can walk behind it — but with a fraction of the crowds.
facts: Walk ~15–20 min each way, a stile and a stream crossing
places.winter: Muddy or icy path; can be slippery in the gorge.

places.name: Sólheimasandur DC-3 wreck
places.note: 4 km walk each way across the sand, or shuttle ~3400 ISK return, runs 10:00–17:00.
places.caution: Long exposed walk; shuttle runs 10:00–17:00 only.
places.summary: The fuselage of a US Navy Douglas DC-3 (C-117) that crash-landed on the black sand plain in 1973 — everyone survived. The stark wreck in an empty black desert is one of the most photographed sights in the south.
facts: Time: ~2.5 h on foot (4 km each way, flat)
Shuttle from the parking ~3400 ISK return, 10:00–17:00
places.winter: Exposed and windy with no shelter; in the dark it is easy to lose the path. Start early.

places.name: Sólheimajökull
places.note: Glacier tongue — you can drive almost to the ice. Don't go onto the glacier without a guide.
places.summary: An outlet glacier tongue of Mýrdalsjökull, the ice cap that covers the Katla volcano. A short walk from the car park brings you to a lagoon at the foot of the ice. Guided glacier walks with crampons start here.
facts: Time: ~1 h to view; glacier walks ~3 h
Signs show how far the ice has retreated
places.winter: Never walk onto the glacier without a guide — crevasses and moulins.

places.name: Dyrhólaey
places.note: Rock arch and lighthouse viewpoint. Upper road is steep and can be slippery.
places.summary: A 120 m promontory with a huge natural rock arch and a lighthouse on top. From here you look along endless black beaches west and across to the Reynisdrangar sea stacks east.
facts: Two parts: lower (beach & arch view) and upper (lighthouse, steep road)
places.winter: The steep road to the top can be icy or closed in high winds. Gusts on the cliff edge are dangerous.

places.name: Reynisfjara
places.note: Never turn your back to the sea — sneaker waves are deadly here.
places.summary: The famous black sand beach west of Vík, with hexagonal basalt columns, a sea cave and the Reynisdrangar sea stacks offshore. Dramatic and beautiful — and genuinely dangerous.
facts: Café and toilets at the car park
A warning-light system at the entrance shows the sea conditions
places.winter: Sneaker waves sweep far up the beach without warning and have killed visitors. Stay well back from the water, especially in winter swell.

places.name: Vík
places.note: Fuel and supermarket. Katla ice cave tours (year-round) start here.
places.summary: Iceland's southernmost village (~300 people): a red-roofed church on the hill, a black beach and views of Reynisdrangar. The last decent supermarket and fuel before the long stretch east. Katla ice cave tours start here.
facts: Good overnight base for the south coast
places.winter: The road east of Vík (Mýrdalssandur) is exposed to strong crosswinds — check road.is.

places.name: Fjaðrárgljúfur
places.caution: Often closed in winter — check before you commit to it.
places.summary: A serpentine canyon about 100 m deep and 2 km long, carved into soft rock with moss-covered walls. A trail follows the rim with viewing platforms looking down into the gorge.
facts: Just off the Ring Road on a short gravel road
places.winter: The trail is often closed in winter and spring to protect the vegetation when the ground is wet — check before you drive there.

places.name: Kirkjubæjarklaustur
places.note: Small village with fuel and a shop.
places.summary: A tiny village ("Klaustur") on the Ring Road between Vík and Skaftafell. Near the village are Kirkjugólf, a natural floor of basalt columns, and the Systrafoss waterfall.
facts: Useful overnight stop for the far east

places.name: Skaftafell
places.note: Visitor centre; Svartifoss hike ~1.5 h return.
places.summary: Part of Vatnajökull National Park, below Iceland's highest peaks. The classic walk climbs to Svartifoss, a waterfall framed by black basalt columns. Another easy trail leads to the face of the Skaftafellsjökull glacier.
places.winter: Trails can be icy. Glacier hikes and ice-cave tours often meet here.

places.name: Jökulsárlón
places.note: 380 km from Reykjavík. Diamond Beach is across the road. Blue ice cave tours (Nov–Mar) leave from this area.
places.summary: A lagoon full of icebergs calved from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier, often with seals swimming among them. Across the road, ice chunks wash up on the black sand of "Diamond Beach". The highlight of the south coast for most visitors.
places.winter: Natural blue ice caves under Vatnajökull can only be visited on guided tours, roughly November to March. Many tours meet here or in Skaftafell.

places.name: Þingvellir
places.note: Rift valley national park. Paid parking.
places.summary: A UNESCO site where Iceland's parliament, the Alþingi, met in the open air from 930 AD. It sits in a rift valley where you walk between the North American and Eurasian plates; Almannagjá gorge is the main path. Silfra fissure, famous for snorkelling, is here too.
facts: First stop of the Golden Circle, ~45 min from Reykjavík
places.winter: Paths can be icy; the open plain is good for aurora on clear nights.

places.name: Geysir
places.note: Strokkur erupts every few minutes.
places.summary: The geothermal field that gave all geysers their name. The Great Geysir itself is mostly dormant, but Strokkur next to it erupts every few minutes, shooting boiling water 15–30 m up. Bubbling hot pools and steaming vents surround it.
facts: Hotel, restaurant and shops across the road
places.winter: Ground around the pools can be icy. Stay behind the ropes — the water is near boiling.

places.name: Gullfoss
places.note: Lower path can be closed when icy.
places.summary: "Golden Falls": the Hvítá river drops in two stages into a deep crevice, about 32 m in total. It is one of Iceland's most powerful waterfalls and the third stop of the Golden Circle.
facts: Free; café and toilets at the top
places.winter: The lower path to the edge of the falls is often closed because of ice. The upper viewpoint stays open.

places.name: Kirkjufell
places.note: Sleep in Grundarfjörður, next to the mountain.
places.summary: The steep, arrowhead-shaped mountain (463 m) beside the village of Grundarfjörður, possibly the most photographed in Iceland. The classic view is from the small Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall across the road. It also appears in Game of Thrones.
facts: Time: 30 min for the photo stop
Grundarfjörður has fuel, a shop and guesthouses
places.winter: A favourite aurora foreground on clear nights.

places.name: Arnarstapi
places.note: Coastal path to Hellnar (~2.5 km).
places.summary: A small fishing hamlet beneath Snæfellsjökull, with dramatic basalt sea cliffs, the Gatklettur rock arch and a big stone statue of the half-troll Bárður. An easy coastal trail runs to Hellnar.
facts: Time: 45 min (1.5 h with the Hellnar walk)
Coastal path to Hellnar ~2.5 km each way
places.winter: Cliff edges have no fences — keep back in wind and ice.

places.name: Djúpalónssandur
places.note: Black pebble beach with shipwreck remains.
places.summary: A black pebble beach in Snæfellsjökull National Park, reached by a short path through lava formations. The rusted remains of the British trawler Epine, wrecked in 1948, lie across the beach. Four old lifting stones once tested fishermen's strength.
facts: Short walk down from the car park
places.winter: Like Reynisfjara, the surf here is dangerous — don't go near the water's edge.

places.name: Blue Lagoon
places.note: 20 min from Keflavík. Book a time slot.
places.summary: A geothermal spa with milky-blue, silica-rich water at about 37–39 °C, set in a lava field on the Reykjanes peninsula. It's pricey and touristy, but very relaxing. Only 20 minutes from the airport, so it works well before a flight.
facts: Book a time slot in advance
Lockers and towels in the basic ticket
places.winter: Since 2023 the Reykjanes peninsula has had repeated volcanic eruptions nearby. The lagoon closes temporarily when there's eruption risk, so check its status before you go.

places.name: Keflavík Airport
places.note: Departure on 8 Nov.
places.summary: Iceland's international airport, about 45 minutes from Reykjavík. Most car-rental returns are close by, with shuttles to the terminal.
facts: Allow time to return the rental car
Fill up the tank before the return

bookings.item: Car rental — Block A (4×4, winter tyres)

bookings.note: Few options east of Klaustur — book early.

bookings.seasonal: Nov–Mar only (natural ice caves). Early-season dates depend on conditions.
Sep–Apr; book for a night with a good aurora + cloud forecast.
bookings.note: Most operators rebook free if no lights.
Pick a slot that leaves time to reach KEF.

links.name: Road status
links.note: Icelandic Road Administration — live road status, closures and webcams. Phone 1777.

links.name: Weather forecast
links.note: Wind is the thing to watch.

links.name: Safetravel
links.note: Alerts; leave a travel plan. Emergency: 112.

checklist: Highland F-roads are all closed in November, regardless of vehicle.
Winter tyres are required from 1 November.
Wind damage is usually not covered by standard rental insurance — check the policy.
Open car doors with both hands — gusts rip doors off hinges.
Check road.is and vedur.is the evening before and the morning of each drive.
Fill up when you can — fuel stations are sparse east of Vík.
Plan to be off the road before dark where possible; keep headlights on at all times (required).
